reasons: Classification is correct: the existing § 14 covenant provides WC, CGL USD 1M, E&O USD 1M and certificates, but no cyber/privacy cover at any level, so it fails the fallback (E&O USD 1M *and* cyber USD 2M) on a material term for a vendor that obtains Company data and may access Company systems — a deviation, not an acceptable fallback.

Redline is a targeted, minimal insertion of a single cyber/privacy limb (USD 5M, conditioned on processing Company data/Confidential Information) into the existing sentence; the rest of the bargain, including WC, CGL, E&O and the certificate mechanic, is left untouched. The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.605 ratio) is not borne out by the rendered text, which shows only an inserted clause.

Sub-elements short of preferred (missing USD 2M CGL aggregate, E&O at USD 1M rather than USD 2M, permitted self-insurance) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the classification rules.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position (USD 5M cyber where the vendor processes Company data) and offers the USD 2M fallback landing zone; it does not misstate the clause.
